newsitem.title: USA: MEHL/Biophile unit's laser gets FDA nod.
newsitem.headline: MEHL/Biophile unit's laser gets FDA nod.

text.p: MEHL/Biophile International Inc said on Thursday its Selvac Acquisition Corp subsidiary received marketing clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for a hair removal system which is the subject of a patent dispute.
The company said marketing in the United States for its proprietary CHROMOS 694 long pulse ruby laser hair removal system would begin immediately.

Palomar Medical Technologies Inc also claims proprietary rights to the hair removal laser technology and said its EpiLaser received FDA clearance on March 10. Palomar said it was issued a U.S. patent protecting the technology.
But MEHL/Biophile contends Palomar infringed on its patented method of hair removal and alleged Palomar marketed its products before receiving FDA clearance. Palomar has denied the allegations.
Palomar said on Wednesday it filed a declaratory judgment suit against MEHL months before MEHL accused Palomar of patent infringement.
MEHL said its SLS Biophile subsidiary has already received approval for marketing the CHROMOS 694 laser in Europe and other parts of the world.
Laser Industries Inc has also said it received FDA marketing clearance for a different hair removal laser, which it called EpiTouch.
Laser Industries licensed the patent for this laser from MEHL/Biophile, MEHL said, adding it then filed a lawsuit against Laser to have this non-exclusive license rescinded.
